overview: Xtep International is a Hong Kong-listed, Xiamen-headquartered multi-brand sportswear company that designs, develops, manufactures, markets and sells footwear, apparel and accessories. Its core Xtep brand targets the Chinese mass market with a 'professional-to-mass influence' running strategy, while Saucony and Merrell (acquired from the former Wolverine Worldwide China business) target premium/professional runners and outdoor consumers respectively. The Group distributes through roughly 8,000 stores (predominantly operated by authorized distributors, increasingly supplemented by a direct-to-consumer push), plus a fast-growing e-commerce channel, with almost all revenue generated in Mainland China and early-stage expansion into Southeast Asia.

business_model.summary: Xtep sells branded footwear, apparel and accessories primarily through a wholesale/distributor network of mall, street and outlet stores, supplemented by a growing direct-to-consumer (DTC) and e-commerce business (over one-third of core Xtep brand revenue). Revenue is transactional/seasonal (wholesale sell-in plus retail sell-through), not subscription-based, with profitability shaped by discounting, channel mix and input/freight costs. The 2024 divestiture of the loss-making K-Swiss/Palladium business (KP Global, sold to the controlling Ding family for ~US$151m) refocused the portfolio on three running/outdoor-oriented brands.
business_model.customer_type: B2C via wholesale distributors, DTC retail, and e-commerce platforms (Tmall, Douyin, JD.com, WeChat Channels); children's line (X Young) targets parents of school-age children
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly Chinese Mainland (plus Hong Kong/Macau); nascent overseas expansion into Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Singapore) and cross-border e-commerce (Shopee, TikTok, Lazada) still a small single-digit percent of revenue

competitive_position.market_position: Xtep is the #4 domestic Chinese sportswear player by revenue, well behind Anta (~RMB70bn+ group revenue including FILA/Descente/Amer Sports/Puma stake) and Li Ning (~RMB29-30bn), and now the weakest performer among the big four listed domestic brands in H1 2026 (the only one with both revenue and profit declines, vs 361 Degrees' steady growth and Anta/Li Ning's larger scale). Xtep brands itself as the #1 running-specialist brand in China by marathon 'wear rate' across major races, a narrower but defensible niche positioning versus the broader-portfolio Anta and Li Ning.

moat_factors.description: Xtep has the #1 wear rate among participants and elite Chinese marathoners across major domestic marathons for multiple consecutive years, a hard-to-replicate perception advantage built over 17+ years of sponsoring the Xiamen Marathon and other flagship races

Saucony's century-old running heritage and Merrell's outdoor credibility let Xtep address premium/professional segments that the core Xtep brand cannot, echoing Anta's FILA/Amer Sports and Li Ning's single-brand-only approach

In-house footwear production (~32% of footwear) plus a new automated Shishi production facility and Jinjiang smart logistics center (robotics, SF Express partnership) support cost control and replenishment speed
~8,000 total stores (6,308 Xtep Adult, 1,455 X Young, 180 Saucony) give broad lower-tier-city coverage that premium/global brands lack

weaknesses: Core Xtep brand lacks the premium brand equity of Nike/Adidas/On/Hoka and is losing share to both larger domestic rivals (Anta, Li Ning) and value-focused 361 Degrees
Smallest scale among the 'big four' listed China sportswear names, limiting marketing/R&D budget versus Anta's multi-brand (FILA, Amer Sports, Puma stake) conglomerate model
Heavy reliance on authorized distributors historically created channel/inventory risk; the ongoing DTC transition is costly and margin-dilutive in the near term
Core brand revenue has now turned negative (H1 2026 Xtep brand -2.2%), indicating the mass-market segment is maturing/losing momentum faster than premium niche players

growth_drivers: Saucony 'premiumization' strategy — flagship/image stores in top-tier malls (including first Hong Kong store, June 2026), expanded lifestyle/apparel lines, and improving store productivity; professional sports segment revenue +11.4% YoY in H1 2026 with gross margin of 55.5%

Structural growth in Chinese running participation and marathon registrations (record turnout at Xiamen, Chongqing, Wuhan, Wuxi events), aligned with the Chinese government's goal to grow the sports industry to RMB7 trillion by 2030
E-commerce and livestreaming channels (Douyin, JD.com, WeChat Channels) growing >20%, now over one-third of core Xtep brand revenue

Channel optimization/DTC transformation — converting distributor stores to direct operation, expanding into shopping malls, outlets ('Xtep Selected' value-retail format) and premium 'Gold Label' stores to lift per-store productivity
New product platforms: '160X' championship racing shoe franchise, value-oriented 'QING YUN' cushioned running line, expansion into outdoor (hiking/trail) and basketball categories
Early-stage overseas expansion into Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Singapore) and cross-border e-commerce (Shopee, TikTok, Lazada), with cross-border revenue more than doubling in H1 2026
Portfolio simplification after the 2024 KP Global (K-Swiss/Palladium) divestiture, redirecting capital/management focus to the three higher-return running/outdoor brands

business.description: Core brand revenue fell 2.2% in H1 2026 (Q2 retail sell-through moved from low-single-digit growth to mid-single-digit decline), and management has guided to a full-year revenue decline for 2026

Anta and Li Ning's far larger scale/marketing budgets, 361 Degrees' aggressive value positioning, and global brands (Nike, Adidas, On, Hoka, Skechers) competing in China's premium running segment all pressure Xtep's market share and pricing
Working capital turnover days rose to 112 in H1 2026 from 90 a year earlier, with inventory turnover days up 14 days to 105, as the company buys back stores from distributors and builds DTC inventory

business.risk: Customer/consumer concentration in a single, slowing brand
business.description: Xtep mainstay brand still ~87% of group revenue; any further core-brand weakness cannot be fully offset by the smaller (13% of revenue) professional sports segment

financial.description: Selling & distribution expenses rose to 24.7% of revenue in H1 2026 (from 21.7%) on higher platform fees, logistics costs and DTC-related expenses (ROU depreciation, staff costs), driving an 11% decline in operating profit and a 2.0pt margin compression
Corporate segment swung to a RMB49.8m operating loss (from RMB18.6m profit) in H1 2026 due to a new share award scheme generating RMB42.9m of SBC expense versus a prior-year reversal
Functional/reporting currency is RMB while the HKEX listing trades in HKD; overseas expansion (Southeast Asia, cross-border e-commerce) introduces incremental FX exposure

regulatory.description: The Chinese Athletics Association has introduced new risk-prevention and operational standards for smaller races, which could affect event sponsorship economics, though large flagship marathons remain oversubscribed

regulatory.risk: China consumer/retail regulation and data rules
regulatory.description: General PRC regulatory environment around e-commerce platforms, advertising and consumer protection could affect marketing and online sales practices

macro.description: Despite stable headline GDP/retail sales growth (China GDP +4.7%, total retail sales +1.3% in H1 2026), discretionary sportswear spending has been uneven, with consumers trading toward value and niche brands rather than mass-market incumbents like Xtep
Broader China macro headwinds (property sector weakness, employment uncertainty) continue to weigh on discretionary retail demand nationally
Rising platform/logistics fees associated with e-commerce growth are a direct cost headwind, as seen in H1 2026 margin compression

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's sportswear/sporting goods market continues to grow at a mid-to-high single digit rate, supported by government ambitions to expand the sports industry to RMB7 trillion by 2030 and rising health/wellness awareness; running and outdoor categories are the fastest-growing sub-segments, while overall industry growth has slowed from the double-digit/doubling rates seen a few years ago
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — consumer discretionary spending on footwear/apparel is sensitive to broader China consumption trends, but recurring participation in running/marathon events provides a more resilient demand base than general apparel
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (net cash balance sheet, modest borrowings); moderate indirect sensitivity via China consumer credit conditions and property-market wealth effects

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: group revenue roughly flat at RMB6,794.9m (-0.6%), core Xtep brand revenue down 2.2% to RMB5,919.9m, professional sports segment (Saucony/Merrell) up 11.4% to RMB875.0m; net profit attributable to equity holders fell 10.5% to RMB817.9m as higher platform/logistics/DTC costs offset gross margin gains (46.4%, +1.4pt)

Management guided to a slight full-year 2026 revenue decline, citing Q3 headwinds and continued margin pressure from logistics and platform fees; Saucony growth decelerated sharply from >20% in Q1 2026 to low single digits in Q2 2026
Saucony opened its first Hong Kong image store at K11 Art Mall as part of its 'era 2.0' premiumization push into higher-tier retail locations

FY2025 annual results: revenue from continuing operations up 4.2% to RMB14,151.1m, record profit attributable to equity holders of RMB1,371.6m (+10.8%), gross margin 42.8%; full-year dividend payout ratio 50.4%

Analyst sentiment mixed-to-positive but trimmed: JPMorgan (Buy, HK$6.00) and Goldman Sachs (Buy, HK$5.70) maintained bullish stances in 2026, while Nomura/Instinet downgraded to Hold (HK$4.20) in July 2026 and CLSA cut its target from HK$6.30 to HK$5.50 (still Outperform) citing a lower valuation multiple (9x vs 10x prior)

Completed divestiture of KP Global (K-Swiss and Palladium brands) to the Ding family controlling shareholders for ~US$151m, exiting a consistently loss-making segment (>US$100m cumulative operating losses) to refocus on Xtep, Saucony and Merrell

Accelerated DTC channel transformation, with plans to convert roughly 300-400 Xtep stores from distributor to direct-operated format in FY2026 and expand outlet ('Xtep Selected') and premium 'Gold Label' store formats

items.notes: CFO guided to a slight full-year revenue decline, citing Q3 headwinds and continued core-brand softness after a roughly flat H1 2026 (-0.6%)

items.target: weakening trend, mid-single-digit decline in Q2
items.notes: Deteriorated from low-single-digit growth in Q1 2026 to a mid-single-digit decline in Q2 2026
Growth slowed from >20% in Q1 2026 to low single digits in Q2 2026 as the brand prioritizes premiumization (higher-quality, lower-discount growth) over volume

items.target: 300-400 stores converted from distributor to direct-operated
items.notes: Part of the broader channel optimization/DTC transformation strategy; also targeting 70-100 additional outlet stores and 20-30 'Gold Label' stores in top-tier cities

items.target: maintained at not less than 50% of profit
items.notes: Interim dividend held flat at HK18.0 cents per share despite the profit decline, reflecting confidence in cash generation and net cash balance sheet (RMB2,326m net cash at 30 June 2026)

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Ding Shui Po emphasized that Xtep's position as China's #1 running brand provides 'a strategic buffer against volatility' amid a tougher macro and competitive backdrop, and reiterated long-term confidence in China's running/sports consumption given government plans for a RMB7 trillion sports industry by 2030. Management acknowledged near-term pressure from rising logistics/platform fees and DTC transition costs but stressed these are deliberate investments in long-term channel quality and store productivity rather than demand destruction.

bull_case: Clear #1 positioning in China's structurally growing running category, validated by leading marathon wear-rate data across major domestic races — a differentiated niche versus broader-portfolio Anta/Li Ning
Saucony's premiumization strategy is delivering high-margin growth (55.5% segment gross margin, +11.4% H1 2026 revenue) and diversifies Xtep beyond its maturing mass-market core brand
Strong balance sheet with net cash of ~RMB2.3bn and consistently high dividend payout (>50%), supporting an attractive income profile even through a cyclical downturn
Portfolio simplification after the 2024 KP Global divestiture removes a chronic cash drain and sharpens management focus on three complementary, profitable brands
Early-stage Southeast Asia and cross-border e-commerce expansion (cross-border revenue >2x in H1 2026) offers a long runway largely untapped by domestic peers
bear_case: Core Xtep brand has turned negative (revenue -2.2% in H1 2026, full-year guidance lowered to a slight decline), suggesting the mass-market segment is losing share to both larger rivals and value players like 361 Degrees

Xtep is the weakest performer among China's 'big four' listed sportswear brands in H1 2026 — the only one with simultaneous revenue and profit declines — raising questions about competitive positioning versus Anta's multi-brand scale and Li Ning's brand strength
DTC/channel transformation is margin-dilutive in the near term (operating margin down 2.0pts in H1 2026) with no clear timeline for when conversion costs will be offset by productivity gains
Rising platform/logistics fees and lengthening working capital cycle (inventory days +14 to 105) signal eroding channel economics as e-commerce and DTC mix shift
Heavy reliance on Chinese consumer discretionary spending, which remains uneven; any broader slowdown in China retail sales would disproportionately hit the already-slowing core brand
